draft.title: Polynomials and their degree
card: A polynomial is a sum of terms, each a number times a whole-number power of \(x\). For example, \(4x^{3} - 2x + 7\) is a polynomial.
An expression is not a polynomial if \(x\) has a negative or fractional power, or is in a denominator or under a root. So \(x^{-1} + 3\) and \(\sqrt{x} + 1\) are not polynomials.
The degree is the highest power of \(x\). In \(4x^{3} - 2x + 7\), the degree is 3.

The leading coefficient is the number multiplying the highest power. Here it is \(4\). Write the terms from the highest power down first to see it. In \(5 + 2x - 6x^{2}\), the degree is 2 and the leading coefficient is \(-6\).
draft.remember: The degree is the highest power of x, and the leading coefficient is the number on that term.

a.q: What are the degree and leading coefficient of \(P(x) = 3x - 5x^{4} + 2\)?
a.why: The highest power of \(x\) is 4, so the degree is 4. The number on that term is \(-5\), including its sign. Choosing \(3\) is tempting because it is written first, but the leading term is the one with the highest power.
a.clue: Find the highest power first, then read the number on that term.

b.q: Which of these is a polynomial of degree 3 with leading coefficient \(2\)?
b.why: In \(7 - x + 2x^{3}\), the highest power is 3 and its number is \(2\), even though that term is written last. The option with \(2x^{-3}\) has a negative power, so it is not a polynomial. The option with \(3x^{2}\) has degree 2, and \(2\) there is the constant.
b.clue: Check every power is a whole number, then find the highest one.
